summary: Monolith Django on Railway with MongoDB Atlas as the database; front end: Django templates + HTMX.

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable Django app: 1 engineer(s) and scale level L1 do not justify splitting services. Microservices rejected: 1 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Server-rendered pages from the same Django codebase, no separate SPA. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Python).

tradeoffs: Highly interactive UIs (drag/drop, live canvases) get awkward.

backend.justification: Ships auth, admin panel, ORM and migrations out of the box. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects; built-in admin/back-office screens. Margin: the full stack scores 12.9 fit points above the best stack built on FastAPI.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).

tradeoffs: Heavier per-request overhead than Go/Node for very high RPS.
